title: With 20 Complaints, Mexico Maintains Defense of 17 Migrants Who Died in the US, Mexico’s Foreign Relations Secretary Says
author: Anahí Del Ángel
content:
_This article by[Anahí Del Ángel](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/anahida/)
originally appeared in the [August 19, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/con-20-denuncias-
mexico-mantiene-defensa-de-17-migrantes-fallecidos-en-eu-sre/), a Mexican
investigative journalism magazine._

The Mexican government is maintaining its follow-up of **17 cases of nationals
who died during operations or under the custody of the United States
Immigration and Customs Enforcement** (ICE), reported the Secretary of Foreign
Affairs, **Roberto Velasco Álvarez** , who noted that the agency filed **20
complaints** before US authorities to clarify the circumstances of each death.

Of the complaints, he specified that eight were filed before **state
prosecutors’ offices** and 12 before **district prosecutors’ offices** in
Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Louisiana, Missouri, and
Texas, the states where the deaths occurred.

Velasco explained that some authorities have only acknowledged receipt of the
case files, while others have already begun to assess possible actions. In
three counties—**Ventura, California; Cook, Illinois; and Harris, Texas** —it
was reported that the corresponding measures will be analyzed.

In contrast, Florida informed the Mexican representation that it will not
carry out an additional investigation in one of the cases, because **its
prosecutor’s office considered that its conclusions coincide with those of
ICE** , stating that it involved a person who **“took their own life.”**

The federal official reported that US$24,788 has been allocated in aid, mainly
for the repatriation of the remains of the deceased, and, in addition, the
**Attorney General’s Office** filed a complaint before the United States
**Department of Justice** to request an investigation, while the **Mexican
Embassy** transmitted the document to US authorities.

Likewise, he noted that Mexico brought the issue before international human
rights organizations. The **United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights,
Volker Türk** , responded to the letter sent by the Secretariat and expressed
awareness of and concern about the situation.

On the matter of legal defense, Velasco Álvarez reported progress in three
cases handled through the SRE’s **External Legal Counsel Program** , related
to the Adelanto Center, California.

He mentioned that in one of them, evidence is being reviewed to determine the
possible liability of a company in charge of medical services; in another,
litigation continues with rulings favorable to the plaintiff and a trial
scheduled for the summer of 2027; while in the third, a possible civil lawsuit
against immigration authorities is being prepared.

As part of the next steps, the Secretariat of Foreign Affairs will continue
following up on the responses from the Ventura, Cook, and Harris prosecutors’
offices, and with special emphasis will press the authorities that have not
yet responded.

The head of the SRE reiterated that **“the defense of the human rights of
Mexico’s migrants is a priority,”** and maintained that handling these cases
does not seek to generate a conflict with the United States, but rather to
exercise the diplomatic, legal, and treaty-established mechanisms to protect
the nationals.
